newsitem.title: USA: FAA proposes new fire safety rules for cargo holds.
newsitem.headline: FAA proposes new fire safety rules for cargo holds.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Thursday proposed new safety rules to require fire detection and suppression systems in the cargo compartments of all commercial passenger aircraft.

The agency also said it planned to ban the transportation of oxidising materials such as the boxes of oxygen-generating canisters carried in the hold of a ValuJet plane that crashed in Florida in May.
Although the cause of that crash has not been officially determined, speculation has centred on the canisters and the possibility that they may have sparked or fuelled a fierce fire on board.
The ValuJet DC-9 plunged into the Florida Everglades northwest of Miami shortly after pilots reported smoke in the cabin. All 110 passengers and crew on board perished.

The FAA said in a statement it was proposing to require the retrofit of fire detection and suppression equipment on 2,800 older aircraft in the U.S. fleet. Currently, most long-range passenger planes, such as 747s, have the systems in their cargo compartments.
"On older planes these compartments have been required to be virtually airtight and lined with fire-contaminant material," the FAA said.
"However, while numerous complex issues remain outstanding, newly conducted analysis has determined that such systems could be extended to all passenger aircraft cargo compartments."
The National Transportation Safety Board has scheduled hearings on the ValuJet crash in Miami beginning Monday.
